reflexion_entries_to_archive.entry: Applying doc corrections via `python -c "..."` inside a bash command let the shell perform command substitution on every backticked identifier in my markdown payload, silently deleting `pickTargetSpark`, `BotGoal`, `serializeSpawner` and ~20 more from 3 lines while REPORTING '4 of 5 applied'. The success count was true and the content was corrupt. Two compounding lessons: (1) for any payload containing backticks, braces or quotes, write a script FILE with the Write tool and execute that - never inline it through a shell; (2) an 'applied N/N' report from my own script is not verification of CONTENT, only of substring matching, so I wrote scan_damage.py to hunt the damage signature (odd backtick counts, doubled spaces, bare empty parens) rather than trusting the counter. I had already hit a heredoc quoting failure earlier in the same session and switched to files once; I regressed to `python -c` two steps later.

My first production-stripping check was `if grep -rl NEEDLE dist/ | grep -v map | head -3; then echo LEAKED; else echo ABSENT; fi`. It printed LEAKED for all three needles with no filenames - because `head` always exits 0, so the `if` ALWAYS took the then-branch. The check could not have reported ABSENT for any input, including a genuinely clean bundle. Rewritten to COUNT files (`grep -l ... | grep -cv '\.map$'`), which then showed 0/0/0. Rule: a verification whose verdict comes from a pipeline's exit status is testing the LAST command, not the predicate. Make the check produce a NUMBER and assert on the number. Corollary that saved me here: I only doubted the result because it disagreed with the +114 B delta I expected - a cross-check from an independent measurement is what exposed the broken instrument.

The bundle after my change was 656300 B against an audit-reported 656186 B baseline. I could have called that 'unchanged' or 'noise'. Instead I moved src/dev aside, git-checkout-ed main.ts, and rebuilt: the baseline reproduced EXACTLY at 656186 B (hash BD5X8Lx1), making the delta a precise +114 B rather than an estimate. That matters because the PDR's headline claim was 'zero production change', and the honest number is 'the harness logic is stripped; a 114-byte empty module record for the side-effect bootstrap import remains'. GROK's R2 attack on that exact claim ('false marketing') was wrong on the mechanism but right to demand the measurement.

Synthetic pointer events on the Pixi canvas did nothing and an async rAF-awaiting script timed out at 30s. Root cause: with the Browser pane not displayed the page does not composite, so rAF never fires and the Pixi ticker - which drives the entire sim loop - does not advance. Static DOM reads (overlay text, window globals, the lambda override) still work fine, which is why the first checks succeeded and misled me into trying clicks. So: DOM/global assertions are available with a hidden pane; anything requiring a FRAME is not. When the game loop is needed and the pane is unavailable, drop to the reducer level - the contract test I wrote instead is deterministic, permanent regression coverage, and strictly better evidence than one browser click would have been.

I ran the S126-S150 -> V6-x.y relabel and the factual corrections in one script, relabel first. That ordering was load-bearing and I nearly got it backwards: several corrections ADD genuine references to the real S126 and S127 (e.g. 'already retired in S126'), and had they landed before the regex pass those true historical references would have been rewritten into V6 slot labels - a silent corruption that greps clean. The header substitution did fail for exactly this reason (its source string still contained 'S126 -> S150', already rewritten), which surfaced the hazard cheaply. Rule: mechanical renames run BEFORE any edit that introduces new instances of the old token, and the rename regex must be range-restricted (S126-S150 only) so historical refs survive.
